- Determinism: faults seed-derived via label-fork PRNG (fork('faults') + per-site sub-forks). fork() never advances the parent, so attaching a fault plan does NOT perturb the topology/ops PRNG streams; clean and faulted runs share the generated scenario, and two faulted runs are bit-identical (proven across an 8-seed sweep + JSON round-trip + public runSimulation).
- Overflow classification: routed ONLY the overflow flood through fireBuffered; every other fire uses a single raw fireEvent classified with origin=undefined, so invalid-event (which shares the {state,event} context shape with queue-overflow) is NOT misclassified as a queue error. The flood reject is classified structurally (event!=='processQueues') under concurrent firing, robust where the per-fire sync-tick heuristic fails.
- AC-4 upgrade (most faithful achievable): the F-Q-1 e2e is now FAULT-ORIGINATED — a throw fault on an onTransition callback produces an errorClass:'injected-fault' frame that a consumer containment invariant (NO-INJECTED-FAULT) detects via PUBLIC runSimulation. The shrinker's M0 (disable-faults) confirms the fault is NECESSARY (minimized scenario keeps faults.length===1; the clean run does not violate), then emitRepro -> re-execute via public runSimulation WITH the record's fault plan re-fails the SAME fingerprint. FROZEN invariants I-11 (injected-fault containment) require the fault to leave internal work pending; a consumer containment invariant on the injected-fault frame is the faithful, reliably-triggerable fault-originated violation through the literal public ./sim path.
